chunks.arabic_text: مَحَاسِنُ الْبُرْقِيِّ: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ الْحَكَمِ عَنْ هِشَامِ بْنِ سَالِمٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ قَالَ

translations.en: Al-Barqi's Mahasin: And from him (Muhammad ibn Khalid al-Barqi) from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Hisham ibn Salim from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

chunks.arabic_text: مَنْ بَلَغَهُ عَنِ النَّبِيِّ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَآلِهِ شَيْءٌ مِنَ الثَّوَابِ فَعَمِلَهُ كَانَ أَجْرُ ذَلِكَ لَهُ وَ إِنْ كَانَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَآلِهِ لَمْ يَقُلْهُ

translations.en: Whomsoever it reaches something about the reward – attributed to the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) – and he acts upon it, he will have the rewards of that, even if the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) had not said it.

en.summary: This hadith from Al-Barqi’s *Ma'ani al-Akhbar* establishes the principle of *mā balagha*, affirming that acting upon a report of reward attributed to the Prophet yields recompense even if the report is not rigorously authenticated as his direct speech. It underscores the Shia scholarly view on the generosity of divine reward for sincere action based on transmitted knowledge, distinguishing between the strictness of legal proof (*hujjiyyah*) and the breadth of spiritual reward (*thawab*).
en.seo_question: What is the ruling on acting upon a hadith of reward if the Prophet did not explicitly say it?
